findings.title: Session type detection calls getUserSession() which can be null for client-credentials/service-account sessions
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() unconditionally calls `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` and then dereferences the result (`userSession.getPersistenceState()`). For client-credentials grants and service-account flows there is no user session (the client session is not attached to a user session), so getUserSession() can return null, causing an NPE during access-token creation for client-credentials — one of the most common grant types. The PR's own example (`trltcc:...` for a transient lightweight client-credentials token) implies client-credentials tokens are expected to be encoded, so this path must handle a null user session (e.g. defaulting to TRANSIENT).

findings.title: GRANT_TYPE attribute set on a DefaultClientSessionContext wrapper may not propagate to the persisted client session
findings.body: In PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process(), the grant type is set via `sessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` where sessionContext is a `DefaultClientSessionContext` created by `DefaultClientSessionContext.fromClientSessionAndScopeParameter(...)`. Whether this attribute is visible later when TokenManager.initToken() reads it via the ClientSessionContext passed to createClientAccessToken depends on DefaultClientSessionContext.setAttribute delegating to the underlying AuthenticatedClientSessionModel notes. If DefaultClientSessionContext.setAttribute only writes to an in-memory map that is not the same instance passed to createClientAccessToken (a different wrapper is created inside TokenManager), the grant type will be lost and the token encoded with 'na'. This path should be verified with an integration test; the unit test does not cover it.

findings.title: Grant maps are package-private mutable fields, exposing internal state
findings.body: grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are declared without an access modifier (package-private) and are non-final mutable fields on the factory. The unit test relies on this to inject state directly. Exposing mutable internal maps package-wide invites accidental external mutation and makes the class harder to reason about; they should be private with the test using the real postInit() path (or a package-private test hook that is clearly intended for tests).
